card.name: Digits before British-spelling units
card.fires_on: Digits inside a number (often the first or second digit) when the next word is a unit like 'per cent' or 'metres', in British-spelled news text. Also a few British-spelled word parts such as 'tum' in tumour.

modes.label: Digits before per cent
modes.description: A digit inside a percentage, where the text goes on to say 'per cent'.
modes.example: the GHG intensity in the US fell by about 1<<7>> per cent, but the total emissions increased

modes.label: Digits before metres
modes.description: A digit inside a length that is followed by British 'metres' or 'km'.
modes.example: 60 feet (1<<8>> metres) high on the northern side.

modes.label: British-spelled word parts
modes.description: Partway through a word whose British spelling differs from American, such as tumour.
modes.example: were 54 per cent less likely to get a brain<< tum>>our, with men 20 per

card.writes: It pushes British spellings like 'organisation' and suppresses American ones like 'favor', 'labor' and 'color'.
card.plain: It spots numbers in British-style news text and nudges the model to keep using British spellings.
